items.title: Is a 3-month model on probation judged like the 6 and 12-month ones?
items.why: You picked "As proposed": a bad week is strictly worse on that week's matured pairs, two must run together, and at 6 and 12 months probation checks clean running only. It does not name 3 months. A 3-month forecast takes about 13 weeks to mature, so forecasts made in the 4 live weeks cannot be scored in them. Proposed reading: pairs exist only from forecasts the model made in shadow at least 13 weeks earlier.
items.today: Admin's Models and evaluations journey draws R1-LGB v2 on India midcap, 3 months, reverted after 2 bad weeks on probation, with matured pairs for the weeks of 19 and 26 October. No record says how long it ran in shadow.

options.because: It applies the bad-week rule you picked wherever there is evidence, and needs no redraw.

options.label: Clean running only, like 6 and 12
options.says: A 3-month model on probation is checked for clean running only, whatever has matured.
options.cost: £0. One rule for every long horizon, but matured evidence in those weeks is ignored, and the India midcap revert is redrawn on a shorter horizon.

options.label: Hold until its live forecasts mature
options.says: A 3-month model stays on probation until forecasts it made live have matured, about 13 weeks.
options.cost: £0. Each leaves probation with a real score, but your 4 weeks becomes about 13 for this horizon.

items.title: May an investment alert ever break quiet hours?
items.why: In the 1 November round you chose quiet hours with approved critical exceptions. On 5 November "Your lines, no investment wake-ups" said critical covers security and service faults only, so investment alerts wait for 07:30. MP-138 still says an alert in quiet hours waits "unless an approved exception applies" and that you approve any exception, which leaves room for an investment one.
items.today: Admin's Alerts and quiet hours panel says Critical: Security and service faults only. MP-138's wording leaves an exception path open.
items.decides: MP-138, material risk alerts, and the delivery policy. The Admin panel's words stand under either option.

Critical covers security and service faults only, so investment alerts wait for 07:30."

options.label: Never for investment alerts
options.says: An approved exception can only be one of the critical security or service faults. Every investment alert waits for 07:30, and MP-138 says so.

options.cost: No work now, but the code keeps an exception path, and the rule becomes a default rather than a bar.

items.title: Which faults are critical enough to break quiet hours?
items.why: Your pick says critical covers security and service faults only, and no record lists them. MP-110 keeps five alert classes apart: financial risk, system security, data quality, billing and job failure. Only a critical alert may push between 22:00 and 07:00. The lists below are proposed.
items.today: Admin's panel says Security and service faults only, with no list. Phone pushes go through Web Push until the Apple programme is bought.
items.decides: MP-138, MP-110, incidents and alert classes, and the Critical row of Admin's Alerts and quiet hours panel on the Admin page.
items.ceiling: £0 a month: no paid channel is added, and pushes go through Web Push, as decided on 3 November.

earlier.words: for the remaining pick up recommended options
earlier.how: your words in chat, 5 November 2026, which picked "Your lines, no investment wake-ups" (MP40-Q11a). The option read: "Material means a line you set is crossed on exposure, price move, volatility or an event flag. Critical covers security and service faults only, so investment alerts wait for 07:30."

options.label: A short named list
options.says: Proposed: a sign-in, passkey or recovery you did not start; a device revoke that fails; production lost (ADM-05); and a failed backup or ledger write. Everything else, such as a missed run or a stalled collector, waits for 07:30.
options.cost: £0. Each named fault needs its alert drawn and tested, and you may still wake for a fault you cannot fix at night.
options.because: It wakes you only for what may need you before morning: someone in your account, or records at risk. Other faults keep until the brief.

options.label: Security only
options.says: Only a sign-in, passkey, recovery or revoke you did not start breaks quiet hours. Every service fault, production lost included, waits for 07:30.
options.cost: £0. Fewest wake-ups, but production can be down all night before you hear.

options.label: Every security and service fault
options.says: Any alert in the system security or job failure classes breaks quiet hours.
options.cost: £0. Nothing waits, but a stalled collector or a retried job can wake you, which the 24-hour repeat rule only partly calms.

items.title: For range forecasts, does the baseline stand in for the rules without a yes each time?
items.why: You picked "Use the best simple baseline" for a task whose rules cannot be fairly scored: the baseline stands in, with your yes each time. Range forecasts are scored by pinball loss, and the rules give no ranges at all, so for those tasks the rules can never be scored. The stand-in would then ask your yes on every trial of every range task. The specification records that reading as proposed.
